title: Choose the visual world for rcfd Studio
question: The roll assigned the Aicher system. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. First surface: the run workspace.

options.label: Aicher System
options.thesis: A strict, friendly system where every run, state and event is a pictogram on one grid and colour is an ordered scale.
options.viewport: Light shell: project rail left, run list with pictogram states, three.js field centre, run-band timeline across the bottom linking residual and monitor plots, Claude Code chat right.
options.risk: Pastel spectrum can read cheerful-soft; state colours must stay unambiguous against it.

raised.raise: Layout reflows by whole grid modules, and the mesh-grid overlay is a first-class toggle state, not a hidden option.
Density courage in the run list and monitors: hairline modules, tabular figures, no card padding inflation.
Selecting a run pulls its numbers into focus while every other run drops to a faint trace.

options.label: Album of Fluid Motion
options.lineage: Van Dyke's photographic plates of flow
options.thesis: The field view as a photographic plate: black ground, white flow, every picture captioned with its numbers.
options.viewport: Dark shell, the viewport bleeds as plate 1 with its caption strip (case, Re, t, iteration); runs as numbered plates in a contact-sheet rail.
options.risk: Familiar: dark viewport plus white captions is where most CFD post-processors already land.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering maps and control descriptions
options.thesis: The solver's field is terrain that nobody edits; your probes, cuts and comparisons ride above it as one reserved purple course.
options.viewport: Viewport fills centre with iso-lines as contours; probes are numbered purple circles with a control-description table beside the run list.
options.case: Fuses strongly on product clarity: data layer never edited by the user layer is guardrail G3 made visible; weaker audience identification.
options.risk: Map palette can fight the field colour maps; purple must stay the only user ink.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each step shows only the decisions ahead: one yellow band tells a learner the next move and how far the run has to go.
options.viewport: A yellow next-step band over a neutral shell: 'Case checked, mesh 8000 cells, start run'; run number and iteration set monumental.
options.case: Holds audience identification (everyone reads airports) and learner-first disclosure; yellow risks costume for engineers.
options.risk: A permanent yellow band can nag experts; it must collapse once a user knows the way.

options.label: Gate Board
options.thesis: Runs rank like flights: a changed state moves its row in place and stays lit until you have seen it.
options.viewport: The run list as a departure board across the top, the selected run as a segmented pass beside the viewport.
options.case: Fuses strongly for the run list (runs outlive the window, state changes held); thinner for fields and learners.
options.risk: Board metaphor covers runs well and fields barely.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The construction grid stays visible as the design.
options.viewport: A poster sheet on a visible grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: a poster grammar, not a working screen.
options.kept: Whole-module reflow and grid visibility as a real state.

options.label: High-density Web
options.thesis: Pack far more on one screen than a Western grid dares.
options.case: Loses both axes: overwhelms the learner-first path.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black and white data at density.
options.case: Loses both axes: no colour breaks field colour maps and state colour.
options.kept: Focus pulls one set of numbers forward, the rest drops faint.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A neutral grey engineering workbench with docked panels and one blue accent, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Outline tree left, viewport centre, property grid right, console and plots docked below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every simulation front end by design.
